directAnswer: St. Pontian was the eighteenth bishop of Rome, from 230 to 235, and the first pope known to have resigned. Exiled to the mines of Sardinia by Emperor Maximinus Thrax, he stepped down on September 28, 235, the earliest exact date in papal history, and died in exile. Tradition holds that he was reconciled there with Hippolytus, the former rival bishop.

sections.h2: Exile to Sardinia and the First Papal Resignation
paras: The Liberian Catalogue, a list of Roman bishops compiled in the fourth century, records that Pontian and the presbyter Hippolytus were deported to Sardinia, an island with a notoriously deadly mining colony, and that Pontian resigned on September 28, 235. The resignation allowed the Roman Church to elect a successor rather than remain leaderless while its bishop was in exile.

The exile came early in the reign of Maximinus Thrax, who reversed the tolerance of his predecessor and targeted Church leaders. Pontian died in Sardinia soon after, probably from the harsh conditions.

Hippolytus had led a separate community since the time of Callixtus. Their shared exile seems to have ended the division, and both men are honored as martyrs. According to Jerome, Pontian had also held a Roman synod that endorsed the condemnation of Origen by Bishop Demetrius of Alexandria.

Pope Fabian later had Pontian’s body brought back to Rome and buried in the papal crypt of the Catacomb of St. Callixtus, where fragments of his Greek epitaph were later discovered. Pontian and Hippolytus share a feast day on August 13.

keyFacts: Eighteenth bishop of Rome, July 21, 230, to September 28, 235
Exiled to Sardinia under Emperor Maximinus Thrax
First pope known to have resigned, on September 28, 235
Reconciled with Hippolytus, who shared his exile
Buried in the papal crypt of St. Callixtus; feast day August 13

faqs.question: Why did Pope St. Pontian resign?
faqs.answer: He was exiled to the mines of Sardinia, where he could not lead the Church. By resigning on September 28, 235, he allowed Rome to elect a new bishop. He died in exile shortly afterward.

faqs.question: Why do Pontian and Hippolytus share a feast day?
faqs.answer: Hippolytus had opposed earlier popes and led a rival community, but he and Pontian were exiled together to Sardinia. Tradition holds that they were reconciled there, and both are venerated as martyrs on August 13.
